reason: Both cover the same core defects (survivorship bias, self-selection confound, mandate-generalization gap, missing uncertainty, multiple comparisons, weak causal link for region, uncontrolled before/after for satisfaction), but Response A's multiple-comparisons treatment is more rigorous, giving both the ~60% chance of at least one spurious hit among 18 tests and a concrete Bonferroni threshold (0.05/18≈0.0028) showing p=0.04 would fail correction, and it closes with a synthesis tying the recurring inferential error together across sections.
